description.value: The Marijuana Craving Questionnaire-Short Form measured self-reported baseline cannabis craving before neuroimaging. It is a four-factor structured scale assessing compulsivity, emotionality, expectancy, and purposefulness; total craving was calculated by summing all items, with scores ranging from 12 to 84. The measure was used to characterize baseline cannabis craving and examine its relationship with cannabis-cue-related brain activation.

model_settings.value: First-level subject-specific general linear models included regressors for cannabis, sexual, and aversive cue conditions, with six motion estimates as covariates of no interest. description.value: Neutral-cue condition: participants viewed 24 neutral nondrug target images, each presented for 33 ms and immediately followed by a 467-ms neutral mask. Neutral images depicted scenes such as building facades and people engaged in everyday activities and served as the comparison condition for cannabis, sexual, and aversive cues.

instructions.value: Pay attention to each picture. There is a small test later to see which pictures you remember.

spans.text: Prior to the task, participants were told the following: “Pay attention to each picture. There is a small test later to see which pictures you remember.”

stimuli.value: Each target image was presented for 33 ms followed immediately by a 467-ms neutral masking image. Targets included 24 cannabis-related images, 24 sexual images, 24 aversive images, and 24 neutral images, presented in two cycles. Cannabis images depicted cannabis, cannabis-related paraphernalia, and individuals smoking cannabis using various modes of administration. Sexual and aversive images came from the International Affective Picture System; neutral targets and masks depicted nondrug scenes such as building facades and people engaged in everyday activities. Images were matched on size, average luminosity, and context/complexity.
